source.title: Constraint-Based Regularization of Neural Networks
source.authors: B. Leimkuhler; Timothée Pouchon; Tiffany J. Vlaar; A. Storkey

record.file_problem: Whole paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares constrained Langevin training with SGD and reports test or validation performance, a different method bearing on generalization under training constraints.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test fitting random labels, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected models, adaptive optimizers, batch size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Its reported test and validation comparisons address effects of explicit parameter constraints and orthogonality on generalization. Values available only in plots are not transcribed as numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether explicit parameter constraints improve held-out performance relative to SGD, which none of V1–V8 claims. Its comparisons contain no random labels, width sweep, controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparison, adaptive optimizer comparison, batch-size sweep, dropout intervention, sharpness–gap measurement, or memorized-example removal. The architectural advantage in V3 is cited as motivation, without an original test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report that appropriately chosen constraints can improve training stability and held-out performance relative to SGD in their tested settings. These results concern explicit constraint-based regularization rather than any of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes constraint-based Langevin training and compares its constrained methods with unconstrained SGD or SGD-m; it does not reproduce a listed original method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies with constraint type, architecture depth, temperature, dataset, training-data quantity, optimizer settings and weight decay; orthogonal initialization worsens generalization for ResNet-34 in the CIFAR-10 setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Orthogonality constraints improve spiral-classification performance for deeper MLPs and improve ResNet-34 held-out performance in the reported CIFAR-10 comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maintaining orthogonality during training can improve held-out performance relative to unconstrained SGD in some architectures and training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: A small temperature perturbation speeds training and often slightly improves spiral-classification test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small Langevin temperature perturbations can improve training speed and held-out accuracy under orthogonality-constrained training.

fits_no_version.finding: Circle-constrained training reaches 87.61% accuracy and 0.386 loss on reduced-training-set Fashion-MNIST, exceeding all listed SGD-m settings, and obtains lower minimum validation losses on both language datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit circle constraints can improve held-out performance relative to momentum SGD in the tested image and language settings.

record.peer_reviewed: OPT2020: 12th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning
record.problems: Several performance outcomes are shown only in figures without numeric values or uncertainty intervals. The NLP table has a text/table inconsistency: the prose names o-CoLA-ud while the table identifies c-CoLA-ud. Comparisons are limited to the architectures, datasets and recipes reported.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance held-out performance for random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification, the contribution of local connectivity, and sparse or convolution-derived initialization conditions.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning dependence, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and recipes that mitigate large-batch penalties.
Dropout's effect, small-data and excessive-dropout conditions, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as a correlate and ranking measure of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions because none measures their effects; this does not imply that the reported method comparisons are unreadable. No additional results bearing on V1–V8 were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization is not tested.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold is reported.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures is reported.
No large-batch penalty comparison or batch-size sweep is reported.
No sharpness or other measured generalization-gap property is assessed.
No removal of memorized examples is tested.

rows.subject: ResNet-34
rows.operation_detail: Trained with orthogonality-constrained underdamped Langevin o-CoLA-ud without weight decay on CIFAR-10; test loss and accuracy tracked.

conditions.value: initial h = 0.1, decay by factor 10 every 50 epochs

rows.note: Text states o-CoLA-ud without weight decay strongly outperforms SGD-m without weight decay; the plot also reports test accuracy.
rows.check: Orthogonality-constrained training versus momentum SGD does not test adaptive optimizers, dropout removal, or any other listed version.

source_check.correct: Initial h = 0.1 is specified for SGD-m. The o-CoLA-ud learning rate is rescaled to match SGD-m parameters and follows the same decay schedule; its nominal initial h is not stated. o-CoLA-ud uses γ = 0.5 and τ = 0.
source_check.problem: The condition assigns SGD-m's initial learning rate directly to o-CoLA-ud despite the stated rescaling.

conditions.value: initial h = 0.1, decay by factor 10 every 50 epochs

rows.subject: 1000-node SHLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained with circle-constrained c-CoLA-ud, τ = 0 on Fashion-MNIST; test loss and accuracy tracked over epochs.
rows.baseline: SGD-m; methods quickly reached 100% training accuracy
rows.value: c-CoLA-ud test accuracy 87.61%, test loss 0.386 without weight decay
rows.note: Authors state c-CoLA-ud is superior in test loss and accuracy; after 400 epochs, its accuracy and loss are compared with SGD-m hyperparameter search.
rows.check: The reported 87.61% accuracy and 0.386 loss are correct, but constraint-based regularization on natural labels does not test V1 or any other listed version.

rows.subject: 1000-node SHLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD-m with and without weight decay; hyperparameter results reported after 400 epochs.

conditions.value: h and momentum settings listed in section C.2

rows.value: Table C.2 gives separate SGD-m values by hyperparameter; for example h = 0.1, mom = 0.8, no WD: 87.39%, 0.824; with WD: 87.47%, 0.531
rows.locator: Section C.2, table of SGD-m results
rows.note: This comparator does not support the constrained method's superiority on test loss for every listed setting; the stated best SGD-m weight-decay value is 0.511, still above c-CoLA-ud's 0.386.
rows.check: Reversed is unjustified. Every listed SGD-m accuracy is below 87.61%, and every listed loss is above 0.386. The note questioning superiority on loss is incorrect. The row also combines multiple hyperparameter conditions and measures; these are comparator results outside V1–V8.

source_check.correct: Every listed SGD-m test loss exceeds 0.386 and every listed accuracy is below 87.61%. For h = 0.1, momentum = 0.8: without WD, 87.39% and 0.824; with WD = 1e-4, 87.47% and 0.531. The lowest listed SGD-m loss is 0.511.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix C.2, SGD-m results table and following paragraph
source_check.problem: The row's note incorrectly questions the constrained method's superiority on test loss; its verdict-fix text correctly identifies this error.
